description: Agent Veterinary Records: submit veterinary prescription records with the animal, treatment, visit and controlled substance log records they answer to: each animal the animal record identifies with its id, reference and name; each treatment or visit entry with its id, reference, the animal, its kind (treatment or visit) and the moment recorded; each prescription entry with its id, reference, the animal, the treatment or visit entry behind it, the medication, whether it is marked controlled, the refills it allows, the veterinarian and the moment prescribed; each refill entry with its id, reference, the prescription and the moment refilled; each controlled substance log entry with its id, reference, the prescription it names, the substance and the moment logged. The signed report gives the prescriptions and the records behind them, each prescription against the treatment or visit entry behind it, each prescription’s refills against the count it allows, each controlled medication against a controlled substance log entry naming its prescription, and each prescription against an animal the animal record identifies, and counts them, and names divergent prescription records: a prescription with no treatment or visit entry behind it, refills recorded past the count the prescription record allows, a controlled medication appearing in a prescription entry with no controlled substance log entry behind it, and a prescription recorded for an animal the animal record does not identify; then a refill dated before its prescription and a refill naming a prescription the record does not hold, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No prescription entries, no treatment or visit entries beside prescriptions, no animal record beside prescriptions naming an animal, or no controlled substance log beside controlled prescriptions leaves those points unverified. Prescriptions, entries, refills and animals match by letters and digits, dates read by the day, a prescription naming no entry rests on a treatment or visit entry for its animal on or before it, and a prescription stating no refill count is not read for refills. This reads a veterinary practice’s prescription record: wever_health-prescription-check reads a person’s prescription against the medication list and the dispensed label, while the veterinary prescription record check reads whether every prescription the practice wrote rests on a treatment or visit, stays inside its refills and, when controlled, reaches the controlled substance log. Verdict vet_prescription_record_divergent, vet_prescription_record_partial, vet_prescription_record_unverified or vet_prescription_record_consistent. POST /api/vet-prescription-record-check. Reads the veterinary practice records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it treats no animal, contacts no regulator, pharmacy or other practice and issues no license, prescription or certification, which stay with the practice, its veterinarians and its regulators, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Veterinary Records reads a veterinary practice’s own records: animal records, vaccination records, treatment records with dental procedures as treatment entries, surgery records, prescription records, lab records, veterinarian license records and controlled substance log records, each against the vaccination, treatment, visit and identity records, the rabies currency dates and booster schedule the record states, the visit, diagnosis, discharge and prescription records, the admission, anesthesia and recovery entries, the refill counts and the controlled substance log, the lab orders, the signed practice records and license classes, or the log’s own totals and inventory counts on record. The family’s ground is the paper trail behind the practice: what the animal record shows, what the treatment and surgery records support, what the license record covers, and whether the prescription records and controlled substance logs hold up; it reads records held by a veterinary practice or clinic, whatever the species, not farm production records and not human healthcare records: the Agent Agriculture Records family reads a farm’s production records, herd treatments the farm itself recorded included, and the Agent Healthcare family reads human healthcare records, while this family reads a veterinary practice’s own records and reads neither. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-veterinary-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-veterinary-records/.

animals.description: Each animal the animal record identifies.

ref.description: The treatment or visit entry reference.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

log.description: Each controlled substance log entry that names a prescription.

ref.description: The controlled substance log entry reference.

controlled.description: Whether the prescription record marks the medication as a controlled substance.

entry.description: The treatment or visit entry behind the prescription reference.

veterinarian.description: The veterinarian, by license reference or name.
